conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces overall risk by cutting leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest growth potential.

balanced.read: This balanced plan prioritizes risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5% per month. It reduces leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech. Expect moderate growth with controlled drawdowns.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the concentration mandate.
Trim SMH to 10% as flagged, but maintain some semiconductor exposure.
Add to SOXL and SPAL, targeting 6% each, to increase leveraged exposure.

aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets ~4% per month by leaning into leverage and concentration. This approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Be aware that leveraged ETFs decay daily, and strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETFs and high-beta exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Trim SMH to zero as it is flagged for trimming and to reduce high-beta exposure.
Reduce CRWD to 5% to minimize high-beta single name risk.

income.read: This income plan aims for ~1% per month by rotating into income-focused ETFs and broad index exposure. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable distributions over growth. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
